title: Nightingale SE daylog — Aurora Health private deploy notes
body:
Context:
- Customer: Aurora Health (regional healthcare SaaS). Regulated PHI flows, must be private VPC w/ KMS-backed keys and audit logging.
- Deployment mode: Redwood Private (customer VPC, control plane restricted via S2S VPN), on AWS account, will optionally test on-prem later.
- Primary ask: predictable latency (<120ms p95 for chat route), per-patient data isolation, audit trail to CloudWatch/CloudTrail -> SIEM.

Meeting notes (2026-03-09 10:00 AM PT):
- Attendees: Maya, Jordan, Lina, Aurora infra team (Sam, Priya), security (Ravi).
- Sam: wants Dedicated-like throughput but insists on VPC peering/no NAT egress.
- Priya: KMS policy must be CMK in their account, HSM optional but preferred for keys used for embeddings storage encryption.
- Action: we provide networking checklist + minimal IAM policy draft by EOD Friday.

Today goals (high level):
1) Finalize VPC connectivity checklist and send to Sam.
2) Confirm KMS key spec and HSM options with security.
3) Draft canary rollout plan for initial 50 requests/sec spike test.
4) Jump into customer's test account to verify subnets and endpoint reachability (blocked till they grant role).

Quick TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Compose VPC checklist (include routes, route table, SG egress rules, allowed CIDR for control plane).
- [x] Review JIRA-INF-3721 (networking ticket) — left notes on required ENI counts.
- [ ] Draft CMK policy sample for Aurora KMS (include key rotation note).
- [ ] Prepare small load script (ab or hey) to run during canary.
- [ ] Add Prometheus alert recipe to the rollout doc for KV cache warmup failures.

Networking checklist (rough):
- Control-plane peering IPs: 10.10.200.0/26 (placeholder) -> need final from infra.
- Allowed outbound ports from customer subnets: 443 to control-plane, 9411 for tracing (if they want).
- Ingress to model nodes: none from public internet; only ALB inside private subnets with TLS termination.
- Route tables: ensure private subnets have route to NAT for updates (if customer allows), otherwise we pre-stage container images in their ECR.
- ENI considerations: 1 ENI per worker per AZ; estimate for 8 vCPUs-ish workers -> request 12 ENIs per AZ.

KMS/HSM notes:
- Customer requires use of a symmetric CMK in their account. We recommend: create customer CMK with key policy that allows Redwood service principal arn:aws:iam::REDDWOOD-SERVICE:role/redwood-controlplane to Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey. (Need exact ARN; placeholders sent).
- HSM note: if Aurora wants CloudHSM backed keys, this increases latency ~5-10ms per encrypt op in our experiments. Recommend HSM only for audit-anchoring keys, not per-request data keys.
- Rotation: enable 1y rotation, mention re-encryption plan for long-term caches.

Canary rollout sketch:
- Phase 0: Infra smoke (agent registration, metrics visible) — 5 min.
- Phase 1: 10 req/sec for 30 min, check p95 latency < 150ms, error rate <0.5%
- Phase 2: 50 req/sec for 15 min, KV cache warmup watch (token reuse metric).
- Phase 3: 200 req/sec for 5 min (if sustained, pause and examine costs).
- Fallback policy: auto-fallback to hosted model variant 'gale-compat' in case of GPU OOMs or >2x latency.

Commands/snippets I keep using:
- curl connectivity test to control plane endpoint:
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redwood-token>" https://controlplane-ep.redwood-internal.example/status

- Quick ab load script (for local smoke):
  hey -n 1000 -c 10 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d @payload.json https://aurora-proxy.local/api/generate

Open questions / blockers:
- Aurora infra needs to grant cross-account role for us to verify subnets. Sam said they will open ticket this week (JIRA-INF-3721 updated).
- Exact control-plane IP CIDR range for peering — currently placeholder.
- Will Aurora accept our request to pre-pull images into their ECR? Legal has to sign DPA for images containing model weights.

Notes to self (time-log):
- 09:15 quick sync with Jordan — confirmed ENI calc and S3 pre-signed length for model artifacts.
- 11:00 spent 30m drafting KMS policy; need review from security.
- 13:45 called Priya about HSM concerns; she asked for latency numbers (send RFC).
- 15:20 created initial canary doc (link above) and uploaded to Confluence draft.

Risk register (handwavy):
- Key risk: customer refuses NAT/egress and also refuses ECR pre-pull -> requires offline image transport, adds 3-5 business days.
- Latency risk if HSM used for per-request data key operations.
- Observability gap if customer doesn't allow tracing egress -> must use push model for traces.

Next steps (by Mar 13):
1) Send VPC checklist to Sam + ask for their control-plane CIDR (owner: Maya).
2) Push KMS policy draft to security for review (owner: Maya, reviewer Ravi).
3) Prepare load script and attach to canary plan (owner: Jordan).
4) Coordinate legal for DPA about pre-pulled images (owner: Lina).

Random scratch thoughts (don't forget):
- Consider doing small tokenized embeddings test on air-gapped mode to check memory footprint differences between q4_8bit and q5_4bit.
- Add a short blurb in playbook about HSM latency tradeoffs so sales/AM don't promise HSM for per-request keys.

End of day note (2026-03-10 18:10):
- Sent VPC checklist to Sam (awaiting reply).
- Security asked to add explicit Allow kms:GenerateDataKey for Redwood role — added to draft.
- Still blocked on cross-account role.

-- maya
